overview: Despatch forwards a 1949 press release: Japanese minesweepers, financed by Japan and supervised by the US Navy, cleared major ports without damage, though magnetic mines still pose some risk through 1950.

people.name: Edward G. Seidensticker Jr.
people.role: Member of the Office of the Political Adviser for Japan associated with preparation of the despatch

people.name: Russell S. Berkey
people.role: Vice Admiral and Commander, Naval Forces Far East

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting press release on mine sweeping
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a Far East Command press release concerning progress in clearing mines from Japanese waters.
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwards a press release on Japan's mine-sweeping progress, naming six cleared ports.

subfiles.title: Far East Command press release, “Mine Sweeping Program Makes Headway”
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.about: The release reports the scope, methods, achievements, and remaining hazards of the occupation-era Japanese minesweeping program.
subfiles.summary: Press release: no ships damaged in Japan's Navy-supervised mine clearance, though magnetic mines remain a concern through 1950.

interest: Shows postwar US-funded mine clearance of Japanese waters using Japanese crews under Navy supervision.
